pages.lesson:
LESSON: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.5: Interactive Speaking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Interactive Speaking. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What strategies can you use to capture key information while speaking interactively?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. utilise the words learnt appropriately in conversations
2. make use of probing to get more information while speaking

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Interactive Speaking helps you communicate well at school and at home.

• Listen with your eyes and ears. Face the speaker and wait for your turn.

• When you speak, use a clear voice and polite words.

• Practise short dialogues with a partner using Kenyan school situations.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short instruction, then repeat it to a friend in your own words.

Example 3: Role-play buying an item at the market using polite requests: “Please…”, “Thank you.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Practise a 30-second greeting dialogue with a partner.
2. Listen to three instructions and carry them out in order.
3. Tell a short news item from your day using complete sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Teach a younger learner one polite greeting from this lesson.
2. Write five sentences you can say when welcoming a visitor at school.
3. Ask a parent to give you three oral instructions; write them down after listening.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Look at an illustration of a family tree and say sentences using the names of members of the nuclear and extended family after a listening prompt (e.g. 叔 叔、表哥、姑姑、堂妹 etc.),
2. Listen to audio recordings about the workplaces of the different family members, take notes, and formulate questions for their peers to answer,
3. Team up with peers to play “Simon says” game where peers listen carefully to instructions and respond accordingly,
4. Learning to learn: the learner reflects on their own work as they provide feedback to their peers on their listening skills and suggests constructive feedback on areas of improvement.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Good listeners look, wait, and respond.
2. Clear speech helps others understand you.
3. Polite language shows respect.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
